Earnings Call Transcript
Bank OZK (OZK) Q1 2026 Earnings Transcript
By

Motley Fool Transcribing

–

Apr 22, 2026 at 11:11AM EST




Image source: The Motley Fool.


DATE
Wednesday, April 22, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET
CALL PARTICIPANTS
Chairman and Chief Executive Officer — George Gleason
President — Brandon Hamlin
Chief Operating Officer — Cynthia Wolfe
Chief Financial Officer — Tim Hicks
President, Corporate and Institutional Banking — Jake Munn
Managing Director, Investor Relations and Corporate Development — Jay Staley
Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email
[email protected]
TAKEAWAYS
CIB Growth
-- The Corporate and Institutional Banking (CIB) group grew by nearly two dozen new client relationships and upsized nearly a dozen legacy relationships during the quarter.
CIB Diversification
-- CIB operates across more than 42 industry niches, allowing the bank to shift growth focus as competition and pricing vary across verticals.
Securities Portfolio
-- Approximately 40% of new securities purchases were invested in municipal housing bonds with tax-equivalent yields near 6%, and 60% in agency mortgage-backed securities with yields at or above 4.60%.
Net Interest Margin
-- Net interest margin was reported at 4.20%, which is positioned above peers according to bank commentary.
Deposit Metrics
-- Despite increased market competition, deposit rates were reduced by 18 basis points, and average depositor balances remain at $52,000, supporting steady deposit growth alongside lending expansion.
CIB Loan Structure
-- Over 97% of the CIB loan book is variable-rate, with the majority of relationships structured for high cross-sell potential and retention of ancillary business.
Efficiency Ratio
-- The efficiency ratio was cited at 39% and is expected to remain in the high-30% range during ongoing business build-out.
RESG Portfolio Appraisals
-- Bank management stated that 50% of RESG commitments were appraised in the last four quarters and 92% within the last eight quarters, with appraisal activity keeping loan-to-value assessments current.
Credit Quality in Indirect Lending
-- Indirect lending, now at 13% of the portfolio, remains high-prime and super-prime, with stable credit performance observed by management.
Loan Syndication Leadership
-- In over 95% of CIB syndication deals, the bank serves as administrative agent, joint lead arranger, or similar lead roles, rather than as a passive participant.
SUMMARY
Bank OZK
(
OZK

0.61%
)
management emphasized ongoing CIB expansion, which is expected to match or surpass RESG by portfolio size as early as 2027, supported by scalable infrastructure and deliberate talent acquisition. Executives highlighted the reduction in deposit costs amid sector-wide competition and steadiness in credit quality across major books, while noting regular appraisal updates that limit risk exposure in the RESG portfolio. Strategic investment in high-yielding securities is anticipated to enhance net interest income, and the growing depth of fee-based businesses—including treasury management and capital markets products—may position the bank for incremental noninterest income contributions beginning later this year. Management reaffirmed that further inflows into substandard credits are likely but expect resolution rates to keep charge-offs relatively contained, with current reserve and appraisal practices cited as mitigating factors.
CIB headcount rose from 18 to 97, with management viewing current expansion as early-stage relative to long-term goals.
Bank leadership said, "CIB is designed so that the speed of that build-out is geared to their volume of business and the profit margins generated by that business."
In the multifamily portfolio, repayments continue to drive payoffs, reflecting stable project performance and moderated valuation changes per management’s appraisal review.
For five specific RESG loans representing the majority of past due and nonaccrual balances, management reported active sponsor engagement on recapitalization, sale, or land disposition processes.
George Gleason stated it remains "agnostic" on near-term interest rate changes due to asset sensitivity offset by deposit and provision dynamics.
INDUSTRY GLOSSARY
RESG
: Real Estate Specialties Group—Bank OZK’s national commercial real estate lending division focused on high-balance, large-scale construction and development loans.
CIB
: Corporate and Institutional Banking—Bank OZK’s group for diversified commercial and specialty lending, fee-based solutions, and advisory products to business clients.
ABLG
: Asset Based Lending Group—A unit specializing in secured, asset-based credit solutions for businesses.
CBSF
: Corporate Banking and Sponsor Finance—Offers acquisition and leveraged finance, often to private equity-backed clients.
NRG
: Natural Resources Group—Lending and services for energy and natural resource sector clients.
LFG
: Lender Finance Group—Specializes in financing to other financial institutions, specialty lenders, and similar borrowers.
Fund Finance
: Business line focused on subscription-based capital call lending and related fund-level financing solutions.
Efficiency Ratio
: Noninterest expense divided by total revenue—a lower figure indicates higher operational efficiency.
Admin Agent
: The lead lender responsible for coordinating a syndicated loan.

Got it. Really helpful color, George. How do you give investors confidence around the pace of growth within CIB and that there is a more differentiated model there as well that we should have the same level of confidence as you grow that this rapidly similar to the results you've delivered in RESG over the life of that business?

Yes. Great question. Thank you for that. I'm going to let Jayse answer part of that question. But before he does, I'm going to tell you a couple of things. Number 1 is talent and leadership are critically important in our company. And Jake will talk a little bit about talent as he answers your question. You're going to focus on a very narrow subset of that universe that meets your criteria for quality of credit, profitability and relationship building, and then you're going to close those transactions with very intentional bank protective documentation, you're going to service and manage those assets in a very engaged way so that you see early warning signs you're able to influence behaviors and move those transactions in a way that is conducive with bank standards and objectives. And 3 years from now, we had the same 2 or 3 verticals every year. The percentage increase from that subsequent addition is going to be less. There are also a lot of geographies that we're not in that we would like to be in with the CIB platform in the markets that we already serve on our commercial community banking business. So there's a lot of room to build out.
And CIB is designed so that the speed of that build-out is geared to their volume of business and the profit margins generated by that business. In the early conversations that Brandon and I had with Jake understood that we didn't want to go out and spend of expense and have a dead start on that, that we needed to take the teams that we had incorporate them into CIB and get them really lined up with the CIB vision, and we needed to add people incrementally as the business was growing, and we were paying for those and creating more profits in CIB. And that will continue to be the approach going forward.
So if I overhead grows 20% per annum. That's going to mean that their revenue is growing more than 20% per annum. So there's going to be a positive operating leverage from the continued growth an expansion of CIB. I would hope and our goal is that is we're building out more infrastructure and treasury management, more infrastructure and trust and wealth, more infrastructure and mortgage that you're going to see the same things. Now we're earlier in the real build-out and expansion of those. But I would expect you would see those gain positive operating leverage as we go forward.
And to the earlier question of where does our efficiency ratio go I hate to apologize for a 39% efficiency ratio, that's a pretty good number. But we would like to see that in future years. Begin to work back down to our more custom ratio over the last decade. But it will stay in that high 30s range this year and maybe into next year, while we're building out some of these businesses. But they are designed long term to achieve positive operating leverage. Now there's no way we're going to run a much expanded trust and wealth business that doesn't have a 50-something percent efficiency ratio or mortgage business that doesn't have a 60% or 70% efficiency ratio.
But the operating leverage that we will get in other businesses, I think we'll even those things out and let us get to a longer-term slightly improving efficiency ratio.

And George, real quick, just to run off of your thought there on CIB. I think it's important to note, too, as we continue to grow and expand CIB, again, the beauty of what we've built. We've got a credit analyst training program as an example in there. So over the long term, you'll see us hiring less portfolio managers as we have analysts and associates coming out of our in-house training.
And so when you kind of put all that together, we ran this analysis at the end of last year, the folks on average we're hiring in this year have a lower average base salary and expense carried than the year before, and we can make the assumption that next year, that will continue to reduce in theory, right, as we're building CIB will need less cheaps and more Indians for lack of a better term. And so we'll continue to staff in that way in a very thoughtful and strategic fashion where we hope to continue to improve the efficiency ratio within CIB itself.
Good comment. Thank you. .

So maybe the best way to characterize it.
